text:
maria: Opening thread for an escalated rerank outage reported by NewslyCorp — they hit repeated 5xx + timeouts on /v1/rerank during a marketing push around 2026-03-15T12:05Z. Customer says they started seeing 504 gateway timeouts and occasional 502s; p95 jumped to ~1.8s from baseline ~130ms.

infra-bot: [alert] prod-eu rerank: p95=1820ms, error_rate=4.1%, spikes from 12:03-12:12UTC

zach-support: Ticket TKT-7190 linked. Customer provided sample payload and said they were sending 90-140 candidates per request, bursts of ~800rps for ~2.5m. They also retried on 504 which increased traffic.

sam-sre: Can we get nginx/gateway logs and rerank pod logs for that window? Also need per-pod restart/oom events.

maria: Gateway snippet from customer: 
```
2026-03-15T12:06:11Z error: upstream timed out while reading response header from upstream 10.2.4.5:8080, client=34.77.21.9, request="POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1"
2026-03-15T12:06:12Z error: 502 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
```

pablo-runtime: Initial hypothesis: large candidate arrays + concurrent bursts causing heavy allocations in the dense scorer path. We have a fallback kernel for small candidate counts; above a threshold we use the "wide" kernel which currently does a single large malloc per request. Under concurrency that hits memory pressure and GC/allocator stalls, causing slow responses and some connection drops (502).

nina-mlops: On the ML side we should check the scorer for numerical instability: division by zero during L2 norm when candidates are zero vectors could surface as 500s. Also confirm whether we have any NaN/Inf logs emitted by the scorer.

maria: From metrics: error breakdown 12:02-12:12UTC: 504=65%, 502=20%, 500=15%. So timeouts dominate.

sam-sre: Immediate mitigations: 1) scale rerank deployment from 3 -> 10 replicas in eu cluster; 2) temporarily increase gateway upstream timeout 20s->40s; 3) enable per-IP / per-api-key burst protection at the ingress LB to cap short spikes. Doing these now.

infra-bot: Executing rollout: kubectl -n inference scale deploy rerank-service --replicas=10 (initiated by sam-sre at 2026-03-15T12:10:02Z)

pablo-runtime: I'll push a hotfix to add defensive guards: return 413 if candidate_count > 80; clamp max processed candidates to 64 for runtime scoring to keep the kernel path predictable; and catch NaN/Inf to return zero scores and log a metric `rerank.sanitized_responses`. Draft PR #3187.

nina-mlops: Good. Please also emit a counter for requests that hit the clamp so customers can see if they're being affected. I'll add a unit test that generates identical vectors and checks normalization behavior.

maria: Customer repro snippet they used (python):
```py
import requests
payload = {"query":"summer jackets","candidates":["c"]*110, "top_k":5}
for i in range(1400):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/rerank', json=payload, timeout=10)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        print(i, r.status_code)
```
They say retries multiplied their effective load.

zach-support: They're paid customer; asked for ETA and RCA. Asked whether we can provide a short-term knob to limit candidate size on their tenant only.

sam-sre: Plan: (a) temp scale + timeout change + ingress throttle (done) (b) land runtime clamp PR and rollout to prod in next 90 minutes if tests pass (owner: pablo-runtime) (c) create tenant-scoped request limit config and offer to enable for NewslyCorp (owner: sam-sre + infra) (d) postmortem in 2 business days (owner: sam-sre).

pablo-runtime: Running load tests locally with candidate=110 at 400rps — reproduces p95 ~1.6s and occasional 502 when concurrent jobs exceed memory. After clamping processed candidates to 64, p95 drops to ~240ms under same load. PR created and CI green for unit tests; integration run in staging now.

nina-mlops: I reviewed the guard for NaN/Inf and added a metric name `rerank.sanitized_count`. Also added a debug log that includes a hash of the candidate vectors for failed normalizations (privacy-safe).

maria: Customer update draft: "We identified that very large candidate lists under bursty traffic triggered a runtime kernel path that caused memory contention and increased latency. We have applied mitigations (scale-up, ingress throttling) and are deploying a short-term limit to stabilize latency. We're offering to enable a tenant-specific candidate cap for you immediately. Full RCA in 2 business days and SLA credit per policy." Approve to send?

zach-support: Send and offer the tenant-level cap. Also request their SDK to implement exponential backoff and jitter on retries.

sam-sre: Telemetry after scale + throttle shows p95 down to 320-410ms and 504s reduced by ~75% in last 10m.

pablo-runtime: After hotfix deploy to prod (canary -> 20% -> 100%) we observed clamps kicking in for ~0.9% of requests; sanitized_count metric reported small numbers. No OOMs in pods post-change.

nina-mlops: I'll run a follow-up test to ensure that returning zeroed fallback scores doesn't cause application errors downstream. We might want to annotate responses with a header `X-Rerank-Sanitized: 1` when fallback applied.

sam-sre: Action items captured:
- Deploy PR #3187 (clamp to 64) and monitor (pablo-runtime)
- Tenant-level cap toggle for NewslyCorp (sam-sre + infra)
- Add metrics: rerank.sanitized_count and rerank.clamp_hits (nina-mlops, pablo-runtime)
- Postmortem draft + graphs in 2 business days (sam-sre)
- Customer comms + credit (zach-support)

maria: NewslyCorp accepted the tenant cap and asked for guidance on how to reduce candidate count — offered checklist and SDK examples. Marking TKT-7190 escalated.

sam-sre: Closing notes: root cause summary for postmortem = combination of oversized requests triggering a non-optimized kernel path that is susceptible to allocation stalls under burst; exacerbated by client retries. Long-term: optimize wide-kernel allocator, add async partial scoring, and stronger ingress backpressure.

maria: Thanks team — will follow up with RCA link in this thread once ready. Closing until postmortem published. :white_check_mark:
